Anton Lundell is day to day and missed their last game.

story.head: The Panthers played last night
paras: The Bruins have won three straight, the last a 6-2 rout of Pittsburgh. The Panthers (9-6-2) lost 4-3 to Washington last night. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Panthers fifth (15th in the NHL) and the Bruins first (tied for fourth). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.
The Panthers’ record (.588) is about what their chances are worth. The Bruins’ record (.735) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.562), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Panthers forecheck harder than anyone (1st) and don't block many shots (31st). They also are the league’s most physical team (1st), so expect a chippy, heavy game. The Bruins have had the league’s best goaltending (1st) and leave the shooting to their forwards (2nd lowest). They also sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (2nd lowest), so the Cats hound the puck, but them sit back. Boston has allowed 2.35 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league.

Matthew Tkachuk (4 G / 21 A / 25 P in 17 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring and is tenth in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games. Brady Tkachuk (10 G / 9 A / 19 P in 17 GP) has a team-high ten goals, with seven points in his last five games. The Bruins’ scoring runs through David Pastrňák (8 G / 14 A / 22 P in 17 GP), who has a point in five straight games against Florida.
Jacob Markström (4-2-1 / .885 SV% in 8 GS) is expected to go for Florida. Jeremy Swayman (8-3-1 / .912 SV% in 12 GS) has been a rock in net for Boston and is expected to start.
At home, Marco Sturm likes to send Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Hagens out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against B. Tkachuk, Bennett and M. Tkachuk.
